[Thinking]
**Gathering boat engine details**

I need to clarify what type of boat engine we're discussing because there are so many variations. I want to gather important details like the engine type, symptoms, maintenance history, and the environment in which it operates. 

It's also crucial to include some high-level troubleshooting steps, such as common issues like overheating or power loss. I should provide the user with a quick-start checklist and safety warnings to avoid any potential damage. Let’s be clear and thorough!
[/Thinking]

I can help, but I’ll need a bit more detail. Boat engines vary a lot, and the right fix depends on the type and symptoms.

Please tell me:
- Engine type: outboard or inboard/sterndrive; gas or diesel; 2‑stroke or 4‑stroke; make/model/year
- What it’s doing: won’t crank, cranks but won’t start, starts then dies, overheats, low power, rough idle, alarms, smoke, vibration
- When it happens: cold start, after running a while, at high RPM, after refueling, after storage
- Recent maintenance or fuel changes
- Any warning lights/codes

Safety first
- If there’s an overheat alarm, oil pressure alarm, or no telltale cooling stream on an outboard, stop running until diagnosed.
- Ventilate bilge before cranking inboards to avoid fuel vapor ignition.
- Disconnect battery negative before working on wiring.

Quick troubleshooting by symptom

No crank (starter doesn’t turn)
- Battery: Check voltage (aim >12.4 V rested). Clean/tighten terminals. Try another known-good battery.
- Kill switch/neutral: Lanyard clipped in; throttle in neutral; try wiggling neutral switch.
- Fuses/relays: Main fuse near battery/engine; starter relay clicks?
- Controls: Corroded ground or loose battery switch; check for 12 V at starter solenoid when key turned.

Cranks but won’t start
- Fuel
  - Primer bulb (outboards) should get firm; if not, check for air leaks at bulb/connectors, empty tank, clogged vent (open cap and try).
  - Water separator/filter: Drain into clear container; look for water/debris. Replace if dirty/watery.
  - Carbureted engines: Check choke operation; spray a tiny bit of starting fluid into intake—if it fires briefly, fuel delivery issue.
  - EFI: Listen for fuel pump prime; check fuel pressure if you have a gauge.
- Spark (gas)
  - Inspect/replace spark plugs; check spark with tester.
  - Kill switch/ignition module issues common; try spare lanyard key.
- Diesel: Bleed air from fuel system after filter changes or if ran dry. Crack injector lines slightly and crank until fuel free of bubbles.
- Compression: If it cranks very fast with no resistance, could be low compression or stuck decompression (diesel).

Starts, then stalls
- Blocked tank vent: Loosen fuel cap and retest.
- Clogged idle jets (carbs): Needs cleaning; can sometimes nurse with partial choke.
- Water in fuel: Replace filters, drain tank bottom if possible, add fresh fuel and stabilizer.
- Anti-siphon valve at tank sticking; replace.
- Idle air control (EFI) dirty; clean throttle body.

Overheating/no telltale (outboards)
- Impeller/water pump likely worn: Replace impeller and housing if scored.
- Telltale clogged: Clear with weed‑whacker line.
- Thermostats stuck: Replace.
- Intake obstructed: Check lower unit water inlets for plastic/weeds.
- For inboards/diesels: Check raw water strainer, belts, coolant level (if closed cooling), heat exchanger for blockage, raw water pump impeller.

Low power/rough running
- Prop damage or spun hub (outboards/sterndrives): Engine revs but boat doesn’t accelerate—inspect prop.
- Fouled plugs, bad coil, or one cylinder down—do cylinder drop test.
- Fuel restriction: Collapsed hose (ethanol damage), clogged filters.
- Exhaust leak or water ingestion (manifolds/risers on inboards) causing misfire.
- Diesel: Clogged filters, growth in fuel, turbo/boost leaks (if equipped).

Electrical/charging issues
- Check alternator output (13.8–14.4 V running). If low, inspect belt, regulator, connections.
- Corroded grounds are common sources of intermittent faults.

After storage checklist (common easy wins)
- Fresh fuel or mix old with fresh; add stabilizer/water dispersant if minor contamination.
- Replace water-separating fuel filter.
- Inspect/replace spark plugs.
- Check/charge batteries; clean terminals.
- Replace outboard impeller if >2–3 years.
- Change engine oil/gear lube (4‑stroke/sterndrive).
- Verify telltale and thermostat operation.

Tools and supplies to have
- Multimeter, spark tester, fuel pressure gauge (EFI), clear container for fuel, basic sockets/screwdrivers, spare fuses/relays, primer bulb/connectors, water-separating fuel filter, spark plugs, impeller kit, dielectric grease, marine grease.

If you share specifics (engine type, symptoms, codes/alarms), I’ll give you a targeted step‑by‑step for your exact setup. Photos of the engine and controls can also help.
